svg.title: LYDEX technology — molecular design schematic
svg.desc: Non-blood-derived two-component design. AD: dextran oxidized with NaIO4 bearing aldehyde (-CHO) groups. SAPL: epsilon-poly-L-lysine whose alpha-amino groups are partly acylated with succinic anhydride (introduced carboxyl groups); the residual amino groups (-NH2) react with AD aldehydes to form Schiff base (imine, -CH=N-) crosslinks, giving a three-dimensional crosslinked hydrogel. Features: adhesion to wet tissue surfaces, rapid gelation on mixing, and self-degradation/solubilization after gel formation (confirmed in vitro). Conceptual drawing, not to scale.

g.text: α-Amino groups of ε-poly-L-lysine partially acylated with succinic anhydride
Simplified notation of the reaction site
Formed by mixing AD and SAPL

svg.text: * Schematic illustration. Chain lengths, numbers of functional groups and crosslink density are not quantitative representations of the actual structure.
Self-degradation and solubilization reflect in vitro findings and do not represent absorption or metabolism in vivo.
